title: loadpath field graph
description: An implicit (field) part, nTop style: named nodes, each a solid (signed distance, negative inside, mm) or a scalar field, where any numeric parameter can be another field.

nodes.description: name -> node. Names are what other nodes and expr refer to.

output.description: The node to mesh (default the last).

groups.description: name -> a reusable sub-graph that `group` nodes copy

params.description: param -> default; the group's nodes refer to it by name

inputs.description: names the group's nodes use for nodes the instance gives

output.description: the node the group stands for (default the last)

bounds.description: Meshing box (default: worked out from the output).

pitch.description: mm grid (default: the box over 4M cells); a third of the thinnest wall or finer

project.description: surface relax+projection rounds (default 3; 0 = raw marching cubes)

decimate.description: mm: thin the triangles wherever the mesh stays this close to the surface (flat and gently curved regions lose most of theirs; creases and small features keep them), e.g. 0.01-0.05

stream.description: write the STL slab by slab without holding the mesh, in bounded memory and with no cell budget: for parts of tens of millions of triangles (fine lattices). Skips the printability check, bodies and the render.

anyOf.description: A name: 316l, abs, alsi10mg, asa, pa-cf, pa11, pa12, pa12-gb, petg, pla, resin, resin-rigid, resin-tough, ti64, tpu, tpu88a (aliases such as 'nylon', 'aluminium', 'steel' work; every value is cited in material_library.py, `loadpath materials`), or a calibrated card measured on a printer (loadpath/calibrations/, calibration.py), which replaces a library card of the same name.

A custom material: E (MPa), nu, strength (MPa), density (g/cm³); or "base": a library name and only the values that differ. EZ and strengthZ are across-layer values, used when the study's process is the one named in "measured".

minWall.description: mm, the printability check's minimum wall (default 0.8)

build.description: build direction for the overhang check (default +z)

editor.description: What `loadpath edit` keeps with the graph (node positions in 'layout'); nothing else reads it.

tune.description: `loadpath tune`: turn these numbers for the lightest part that still meets the study's limits, each candidate meshed and analyzed (tune.py)

study.description: study JSON path or example:<name>: loads, supports, material, goal

also.description: numbers that move with it ('-' first: the other way)

safetyFactor.description: least safety factor (default the study's goal)

maxDeflection.description: mm at the loads (default the study's goal)

sweep.description: the trade-off: tune again held to each of these values of one limit, e.g. {"maxDeflection": [0.4, 0.6, 0.8]}

analysis.description: auto (default): a part with a lattice is analyzed with the lattice homogenized (unit-cell stiffness and wall stress), else meshed and verified as a solid

envelope.description: solid node the lattice core fills (the crush pad)

density.description: relative density: a scalar node (the one the lattice node uses) or a number (default 1 = solid)

energy.description: J, instead of mass and velocity

forceLimit.description: N, the most the part behind may feel

grade.description: also work out the flattest graded core for this envelope and give it as a density remap table

rhoMin.description: lowest printable relative density for grading (default 0.12)

cell.description: mm lattice cell: with minWall, raises rhoMin to the thinnest printable wall

impact.description: Crush and impact of a lattice core (impact.py): force-crush curve, where a mass at a speed stops, peak force and g, and with grade a density table that crushes every layer at the same force. Needs material.

density.description: relative density node or number (default 1 = solid)

fixed.description: solid node: nodes inside it are clamped

region.description: solid node the mass attaches over

minFrequency.description: Hz the first mode must clear

excitation.description: Hz of a known shake: reports the worst transmissibility

vibration.description: Natural frequencies, effective masses and damping (modal.py). Needs material.

buildDirection.description: the direction layers stack: '+z', a vector, or 'auto'

minHole.description: mm: narrowest hole or gap the optimizer may leave (default FDM/SLS/MJF 2, SLA/DLP/LPBF 1, volumetric 0.6)

escapeHole.description: mm: smallest powder escape / resin drain hole (default SLS 4, MJF 5, SLA/DLP 3.5)

process.description: How it is made: sets the minimum wall, the build direction and the drain holes (sls, mjf, sla, dlp, volumetric, lpbf drain sealed voids by default).

diameter.description: mm (default 1.5 x the process's minimum escape hole or 2 mm over it, whichever is larger: SLS 6, MJF 7.5, SLA/DLP 5.5, volumetric 5; LPBF 6.8, an M8 tap drill)

count.description: holes per void (default 2: one low, one high along the build)

stress.description: node that ranks the sites, calmest first (default the first result node; null: none)

boss.description: mm of solid round each hole (default max(1.5 x min wall, 0.4 x radius))

blend.description: mm fillet boss to part (default the boss wall)

maxDepth.description: mm: sites at most this far under the outside (default 6)

fillBelow.description: mm^3: smaller voids are filled solid (default the escape ball)

keepClear.description: solid nodes the bosses stay out of (bearing seats, mating faces)

pitch.description: mm grid for finding voids (default the mesh pitch)

maxPath.description: mm: add holes (up to 8 a void) while any powder is farther than this from a hole, through the void (default 60; null: just count)

drains.description: Drain holes into sealed voids (trapped powder or resin): 'auto' (default) drills for powder-bed and resin processes, true always, false never. Holes go at the calmest flat sites, each on a solid boss; pockets too small for a hole are filled; the report says what (if anything) is still sealed.

box.description: Axis-aligned box: min/max corners, or center/size.

cylinder.description: Cylinder or tube: end points p0/p1, or center/axis/length; radius r, optional rInner.

mesh.description: A closed mesh: an STL/3MF/OBJ path relative to the study's folder, or inline stlBase64.

union.description: Several shapes acting as one region (a servo's four screw bosses).

shape.title: a shape object (box, cylinder, tube, sphere, mesh, union)
shape.description: A shape: box, cylinder (tube), sphere, mesh or union. Units mm.

node.title: a node object with an 'op'
node.description: A field node: constant, coordinate, distance, shape, mesh, result, grid, image, remap, expr, union, intersect, subtract, shell, offset, lattice, transform, group.

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-coordinate.description: Position along an axis (mm): 'x', 'y', 'z', or a direction from `origin`.

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-distance.description: Unsigned distance (mm) to a solid's surface (`input`), to points, a segment, a plane or a shape. The usual driver of a ramp: thicker near the bolts, finer cells near the load.

input.title: a number, a node name or a node object
input.description: A number, the name of another node, or an inline node object: anywhere a number goes, a field can drive it.

signed.description: with input: keep the sign (negative inside)

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-shape.description: An exact primitive solid (box, cylinder, tube, sphere, union), as in a study.

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-mesh.description: A closed mesh (STL/3MF/OBJ) as a solid: exact distance near its surface, so it re-meshes smooth.

source.description: an in-memory mesh passed to FieldGraph(meshes=)

band.description: mm from the surface within which distance is exact (default 3 pitches); make it cover shell thicknesses

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-result.description: A simulation result as a scalar field: von Mises stress (MPa) or displacement (mm) of `part` under `study` (analyzed on demand), a saved .npz (points + values, or verify fields), or an in-memory source.

path.description: .npz with points and values (save_result_field) or a grid (origin, pitch, values)

study.description: study JSON, relative to the graph's folder, or 'example:<name>' for a packaged example

part.description: the mesh the study analyzes, or the name of a node of this graph (meshed for the analysis)

pitch.description: mm, meshing a node part for the analysis (default 1)

quantity.description: vonMises (default) or displacement for a study; the array name in an .npz

case.description: one load case (default: the worst at each point)

scale.description: divide by this, or 'peak' (the 99.5th percentile): remap in fractions of the part's own worst stress

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-grid.description: An imported scalar field on a regular grid (.npz with origin, pitch, values[nx,ny,nz]): a temperature map, a CFD pressure, a hand-painted density.

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-image.description: A picture as a scalar field from 0 to 1, laid on a plane and carried straight through along the third axis: a logo to emboss, a texture to drive a wall, a hand-painted density.

path.description: PNG, JPEG, ... in the graph's folder

plane.description: the plane it lies in (default xy)

origin.description: lower-left corner in the plane, mm (default [0, 0])

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-remap.description: Map `input` from [a, b] to [c, d] through a curve (clamped unless clamp is false). Longer from/to lists are a piecewise-linear table (from ascending), e.g. a density per height for an impact core.

input.title: a number, a node name or a node object
input.description: A number, the name of another node, or an inline node object: anywhere a number goes, a field can drive it.

anyOf.description: points [u, v] over the unit square, u ascending from 0 to 1: a drawn curve

bounds.description: Where this solid lives, when it cannot be worked out (meshing needs the output's).

op-expr.description: Arithmetic over node names, x, y, z, pi, e and abs sqrt exp log sin cos tan floor ceil sign min max clamp lerp smoothstep step where, e.g. '0.8 + 1.2 * smoothstep(5, 30, stress)'.
